extracted.intended_audience: researchers / PIs and research teams applying to the Schmidt Sciences Science of Trustworthy AI funding program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting research proposals to the Science of Trustworthy AI program (eligibility, budgeting, team composition, international award rules, allowable uses, and submission rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: organizational status (501(c)(3) or equivalent)
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient of funding must hold a 501c3 designation or equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible entities include: Individual researchers or project teams at universities or research institutions (including international institutions); non-profits, research organizations or agencies; multi-institution collaborations between universities and/or non-profits; non-profits and/or universities with partnerships with industry or for-profits. For-profits cannot lead awards (see separate entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: For-profit entities may not lead awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial (for‑profit) entities cannot apply to lead projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For‑profit companies may partner with consortiums of researchers, academics, and other parties that hold a 501(c)(3) designation or equivalent, but may not be the award recipient/lead institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: 501(c)(3) status timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants do not need 501(c)(3) status at application time, but must have obtained it by the final stage of project selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your organization will be able to obtain required status prior to final selection to avoid disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team may submit multiple proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: A PI or team may submit more than one proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no limit preventing multiple submissions from the same PI or research team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition should demonstrate capacity and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no strict team-size rules, but proposals should illustrate the team's capacity to complete the project and necessary subject-matter expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the team to show you can meet project goals and have technical/content expertise; quality matters more than headcount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Junior faculty competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Junior faculty may apply for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Junior applicants must clearly demonstrate their ability to make a successful impact on the project goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-institutional collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-institution collaborations are welcome at all levels of funding but are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborations are encouraged but not mandatory; multi-institution projects are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdocs may be hired at project start
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects may hire postdoctoral researchers at the project's start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including postdocs in staffing plans is permissible; budget accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out-of-scope: policy-adjacent advocacy research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research whose outcomes are focused on advocating for specific policy or legislation is out of scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should avoid framing outcomes as advocacy for particular policies/legislation; policy‑adjacent analysis that does not advocate may be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs cap (overhead)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs must not exceed 10% for the entire project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for a $1,000,000 award, indirect costs should not exceed $100,000. Budget indirects accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directly incurred staff salaries allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocated and directly incurred staff salaries may be included in the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include personnel costs for staff as direct costs where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding may support PhD students
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds can be used to support PhD students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use award funds to support graduate students as part of project staffing and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: No co-funding requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant may cover the entire project cost; co-funding is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may request full project support without needing matching funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: No‑cost extensions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No‑cost extensions will be evaluated on a case‑by‑case basis and are not guaranteed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose projects that can be completed within the stated timeframe; do not assume extensions will be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution / payment preference
rubrics_metrics.description: The institutional home of the lead PI is considered the 'host' institution for the award; Schmidt Sciences prefers funding to go directly to the host.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer that the lead host receives all funds and issues subawards to co‑hosts; splitting into separate awards is possible but less preferred. Only total subaward amounts need to be reported to Schmidt Sciences. Hosts are expected to actively manage subawardees and review reports to ensure alignment with program guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second‑tier subawards permitted but recipient-managed
rubrics_metrics.description: Second‑tier subawards are allowed if the recipient is comfortable managing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and ongoing management of second‑tier subawardees is the responsibility of the award recipient organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gift vs grant structure and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding may be structured as gifts or grants; gifts generally have less administrative burden and reporting, while grants include customary contractual provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gifts are provided via a simple letter and may be advantageous; grants include agreements with clauses on governing law, IP, indemnification, etc. If a gift structure imposes administrative burden, Schmidt Sciences will discuss a grant structure instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi‑year funding delivered as contingent annual gifts/grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Large multi‑year projects are funded as a series of one‑year gifts (or grants) based on reported progress and plans; future years are anticipated based on scientific progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual continuation is contingent on progress reported in annual narrative and financial reports. Schmidt Sciences can adapt letters/agreements where required by local laws or university policies (e.g., front‑loading for specific hiring/legal requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award period alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Award periods do not necessarily align with calendar years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that project year boundaries may differ from calendar years when planning schedules and budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: International direct award: governing law and ED status
rubrics_metrics.description: Gift letters generally contain no explicit reference to U.S. governing law aside from ED (equivalency determination) status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect gift letters to be structured without asserting U.S. governing law except where ED requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: International equivalency (ED) requirement and NGOSource process
rubrics_metrics.description: Schmidt Sciences will evaluate international direct funding recipients' equivalence to a U.S. 501(c)(3). If needed, they will determine equivalency via NGOSource and request organization information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schmidt Sciences covers ED processing costs and currently works exclusively with NGOSource; prior EDs via other organizations may not substitute. The ED process can take up to 90 days; institutions must be responsive to NGOSource requests to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on allowable uses (legal/regulatory limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions include those required by applicable law and regulations, including activities in sanctioned nations; beyond legal restrictions, awards are intended to provide relatively flexible funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of funds must comply with laws and sanctions. Otherwise, the program aims to be flexible to support international partners and scientific collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of commonly allowable uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously awarded projects used funds for grad students, postdocs, other scientists, conferences, meetings/exchanges, software engineering support, cloud computational infrastructure (compute/GPU, storage), and other standard research expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for personnel, collaboration facilitation, software/engineering, and cloud resources as typical allowable expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large equipment in budget and ownership/depreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Large scientific equipment can be included in the budget; equipment will not belong to Schmidt Sciences and equipment depreciation calculation is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If funded, ownership typically follows the lead institution's policies. Depreciation may be included at proposer's discretion but is not mandated by Schmidt Sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on award dollars for US travel by international recipients & tax withholding
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants to overseas institutions are not generally subject to US tax withholding provided the recipient does not use the funds for activities in the U.S.; using award funds for US travel may trigger withholding considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is often more cost‑effective for non‑US recipients to fund US travel from non‑Schmidt sources. If US activities are essential, contact Schmidt Sciences to discuss options. Providing Form W‑8EXP or W‑8BEN‑E may evidence that US tax withholding is not required. These rules apply equally to grants and gifts to non‑US awardees.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI assistance in proposal drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: AI may assist in drafting proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs are ultimately responsible for the accuracy of their proposals even if AI tools are used; verify and take ownership of all content submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of support are not required and will not be reviewed or accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include letters of support in submissions; they will not be considered.
